item.title: NFL Makes Final Decision on Punishment for ‘Dirty’ Travis Kelce Hit
item.description: Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce hits a huge record before suffering an ankle injury against the Falcons. Getty Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce shared his thoughts on what some fans thought was a “dirty” hit that left him briefly injured against the Atlanta Falcons last week, and the NFL has now had its final say on the play. Kelce was hurt after Atlanta Falcons safety DeMarcco Hellams tackled him low, aggravating an already injured ankle. There was some speculation that Hellams may have intentionally tried to injure Kelce, and the Chiefs tight end would not say one way or the other. But the league decided on Saturday that Hellams did not run afoul of any rules with the hit. NFL Decides Against Fine for Falcons Player The NFL announced fines for all Week 10 games on Saturday, with nothing listed for the Falcons in their loss to the Chiefs last week. Kelce had addressed the hit on his “New Heights” podcast this week, answering a question from a fan who called the hit “dirty.” “I don’t know if that was the case; the way he tackled me… and I just got caught in a bad position,” Kelce replied. “You know, that’s football. And on the flip side, you know, if it was a quote-unquote intentional, you know, extra grab and turn of the ankle, you know, it’s just part of it.” Kelce agreed that the play did not warrant a flag, as Hellams made a legal hit, but said it did leave him hurt. The Chiefs tight end was in visible pain and briefly left the game, but was able to return. “I don’t think it was, you know, crazy enough for it to get a flag or it to be a fine or anything like that,” Kelce said. “Obviously, in the moment, I thought it was, because it hurt like hell.” Chiefs Have Chance to Make Up Ground The Chiefs have turned their attention to Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals, where they will face a well-traveled veteran quarterback. The Cardinals ruled out Carson Beck, handing the ball instead to Josh Johnson. Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur shared praise for the 40-year-old. “You’ve got to have a baseline talent level, which clearly half the league has felt like [Johnson] has,” LaFleur said. “He is incredible in the quarterback room. He’s incredible for the starter. He’s incredible for young quarterbacks in terms of just the way he sees the game, his energy, his positivity, how he keeps it real. He’s mature, and he can still sling it. He’s been in this league. It’s not like he was just on the street.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post NFL Makes Final Decision on Punishment for ‘Dirty’ Travis Kelce Hit appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Defense Carries Irish Over SMU
item.description: Notre Dame’s defense made key stops in critical moments as the Irish won by 24-3 on Senior Night. SMU’s potent offense poked holes in Notre Dame throughout the evening but failed to breach the goal line. CJ Carr and the Irish attack sputtered at times and stopped themselves with two careless turnovers. Several explosive plays were the difference in the game as Carr hit long passes to multiple receivers. The win moves Notre Dame to 10-1 on the season on a wild day of upsets in college football. SMU stunned the Irish on the opening series when Kendrick Raphael broke off a 70-yard run to reach the red zone. Notre Dame held but paid a heavy price as Luke Talich suffered a significant injury defending a pass. Kicker Brendan Baird came on to put the Mustangs on the board with a short field goal. A fumbled snap blew up the play and the Irish took over. Carr moved the hosts and found Jordan Faison across midfield. Faison lost the ball while fighting for additional yards and SMU recovered. It seemed then as though it was going to be one of those ugly games. The Mustangs could not capitalize but caught a break when their punt came to rest on the Irish one. Jaden Greathouse caught the first of several deep throws by Carr and rambled 62 yards. A pass interference penalty set up a short scoring run by Cooper Flanagan from a full house backfield. This capped a 99-yard drive and an anxious crowd breathed a sigh of relief. Quarterback Kevin Jennings and the Mustangs responded as the game moved into the second period. The drive ran out of gas in Irish territory as Baird nailed a 40-yard field goal. This cut Notre Dame’s advantage to 7-3. Carr looked to Faison as the Mustang defense began loading up against the run. They connected for 31 yards before Faison made a spectacular one-handed touchdown catch on a corner route. Jordan Faison (6) had a great night against SMU (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire) Trailing by 14-3, Jennings rallied his team by hitting Yamir Knight for 34 yards to reach Irish territory. A few plays later, Jennings went for broke and lofted a long pass to Jalen Cooper near the pylon. Irish cornerback Jaylen Sanders made a leaping interception and fell into the end zone. The teams exchanged punts before Notre Dame took over with 34 seconds remaining in the half. Carr hit Jack Larsen for 25 yards and Micah Gilbert for 37 more as the seconds ticked away. After yet another fade pass fell harmlessly to the turf, the Irish settled for a Spencer Porath field goal. This stretched their lead to 17-3 as the half ended. Notre Dame received the kickoff to open the third quarter and started fast. Nolan James ripped off a 38-yard run into the Mustang red zone. James completed the drive moments later with a four yard touchdown burst. The score stood at 24-3 with over 25 minutes remaining in the game. No one could have guessed these would be the last points of the night. Later in the period, Jennings hit Knight for a long gain to the Irish five yard line

Jordan Faison (6) had a great night against SMU (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire) Trailing by 14-3, Jennings rallied his team by hitting Yamir Knight for 34 yards to reach Irish territory. A few plays later, Jennings went for broke and lofted a long pass to Jalen Cooper near the pylon. Irish cornerback Jaylen Sanders made a leaping interception and fell into the end zone. The teams exchanged punts before Notre Dame took over with 34 seconds remaining in the half. Carr hit Jack Larsen for 25 yards and Micah Gilbert for 37 more as the seconds ticked away. After yet another fade pass fell harmlessly to the turf, the Irish settled for a Spencer Porath field goal. This stretched their lead to 17-3 as the half ended. Notre Dame received the kickoff to open the third quarter and started fast. Nolan James ripped off a 38-yard run into the Mustang red zone. James completed the drive moments later with a four yard touchdown burst. The score stood at 24-3 with over 25 minutes remaining in the game. No one could have guessed these would be the last points of the night. Later in the period, Jennings hit Knight for a long gain to the Irish five yard line. Remarkably, the defense dug in and forced incompletions on third and fourth downs. It appeared Notre Dame would embark on another long scoring drive after securing a pair of first downs. It was not to be. Carr got greedy as he bypassed an open receiver to take a deep shot into coverage. Jayvon Thomas intercepted it on the first play of the final quarter. The Irish defense frustrated Jennings and the Mustangs once again as Elijah Hughes recorded a 13-yard sack. SMU punted the ball to the Notre Dame three yard line. When the Irish fell short on third down, punter Jasper Scaife blasted a 76-yard bomb. It was not returned. Jennings would not go away quietly. Aided by a pair of 15-yard penalties against the Irish, SMU returned to the red zone. Notre Dame rallied for one final stand to keep the Mustangs out of the end zone. Four consecutive passes by Jennings yielded only three yards. The Irish again took over in the shadow of their own goal and proceeded to run out the clock. Jaden Greathouse suffered a wrist injury (Photo by Brian Spurlock/Icon Sportswire) Despite 312 passing yards by Carr and 152 more on the ground, it was hardly a satisfying performance. Turnovers and costly penalties have become more commonplace. Carr’s penchant for ignoring open receivers to make low percentage home run throws is somewhat concerning. A larger issue is the injuries that are piling up. Talich is likely lost for the season and Greathouse left the game with a wrist injury. His replacement, Mylan Graham, cannot seem to connect with Carr despite being open. Star linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa also departed early with an apparent injury. Let us review the answers to our pregame questions: Can SMU’s struggling offensive line give Jennings a chance to shine? Jennings was a mediocre 24 of 45 for 216 yards and one interception. He hit some big plays but was terrible in the red zone where Notre Dame turned up the pressure. Will Notre Dame exceed 200 yards rushing? No. SMU took away the run for the most part except for one long gain by James. He finished with 98 yards on 15 carries. Can the Irish secondary cover the Mustang receivers and tight ends? Coverage was shaky at times. Pressure on Jennings forced him to miss open receivers. Also, Irish cornerback Christian Gray had a rough night. Talich usually erases a number of mistakes on the back end. He spent most of the night on the sideline in a boot. Will Carr use play-action to set up explosive passing plays? I did not see much play-action. Mostly, CJ just chucked it downfield with mixed results. Can White and the SMU pass rushers get past the Irish offensive line? SMU earned one sack that was attributable to good coverage downfield. Otherwise, Carr had time to throw without pressure. Will Brewu, Jagusah, or Johnson make a splash upon their return? Brewu and Jason Onye had a few snaps and held up well. Jagusah got on the field to block for extra points and in victory formation. Johnson did not play, largely because Talich got hurt. It was not worth the risk to put Johnson out there. Can Notre Dame’s special teams make a meaningful contribution? Scaife’s 76-yard punt was memorable. The Irish responded well when SMU tried to advance the ball on a botched field goal attempt. Will a convincing win by the Irish drop them out of the playoffs? Notre Dame was never in danger but the Committee will almost certainly denigrate their performance. They are rapidly running out of mediocre teams to put ahead of the Irish, though. A few players stood out with excellent performances. Faison made up for an early fumble with seven receptions for 109 yards and an amazing touchdown. The pass blocking was excellent once again. Kudos to the linemen including Owen Strebig, who filled in for Will Black. On defense, Sanders played well as did Viliamu-Asa. Finally, Boubacar Traore was the star of the show for the Irish. NFL scouts are going to love his film from this game. It was a rough day for several teams. UCLA lost its first game and also their quarterback. Indiana fell to Washington and lost star receiver Nick Marsh and a starting offensive lineman. Ohio State has simply lost its way. Notre Dame avoided losing this game but the attrition on defense is alarming. Next week’s regular season finale at Syracuse should be an opportunity to rest key starters. Hopefully, the loyal Irish fan base will be able to relax as well. It has been a stressful second half of the season. The post Defense Carries Irish Over SMU appeared first on NDNation .

item.title: 'He will see what Man Utd are made of' - Pulis on Pochettino's first game
item.description: [BBC] Stepping into a job like Mauricio Pochettino has done at Manchester United, where managers have come and gone frequently, will always lead you to wonder why the others have not lasted very long. Irrespective of results, you face these first few days in your new post with suspicion. So, while what happens in Pochettino's first game against Liverpool on Sunday is important, it will not define his early opinions of the club - good or bad. Whenever you take over a team in mid-season, which I did on a few occasions, you don't usually get much time to work with your players before your first game. Jumping straight in and going straight to the heart of a two-day preparation for a game, like Pochettino has done before United go to Anfield, is so difficult and I am not sure any manager can honestly make a profound difference. A change of voice helps, I'm sure, but so does showing strength and confidence in your own principles and making sure the players understand you demand complete and utter commitment in all the games you face, starting with this one. With time on the training ground being so limited, my initial work would focus on us being a team and working up and down the pitch together, by breaking down different scenarios inside the game and what we should do in them. I'd keep the focus on hard work and making us difficult to beat - clean sheets are so under-rated. Then, on the day, your first pre-match speech is always a massive one, and it will be the same for Pochettino too. My first team talk would always focus on generating an 'us against the world' mentality. As a manager coming in now, you've usually got the job because the team has struggled, so you can play on that to motivate the players. You can use media reports and stories to show the negativity against them - but then counter that by producing a real 'stand-up and be counted' kind of rallying call, before sending them out on the pitch, while mentioning your faith in them to succeed. Pochettino had his first training session with United's players on Thursday [Getty Images] 'What your own eyes tell you is most important' I would have selected my team before I met the players, through my own knowledge and also with help from within. Whichever club I went in at, I'd expect to know something about most of the players within the group in terms of their position and ability, but understanding the character of the squad was vital too. The existing staff would know more about the lads' qualities in that respect than myself or anyone who had just arrived with me, so I'd always discuss that with the people I had inherited, from fitness coaches to the medical department. It's what your own eyes tell you that is most important, however. Going into your first game gives you the opportunity to see for yourself what your players are made of - and it can be a completely different view from what other people see. item.content:encoded: [BBC] Stepping into a job like Mauricio Pochettino has done at Manchester United, where managers have come and gone frequently, will always lead you to wonder why the others have not lasted very long. Irrespective of results, you face these first few days in your new post with suspicion. So, while what happens in Pochettino's first game against Liverpool on Sunday is important, it will not define his early opinions of the club - good or bad. Whenever you take over a team in mid-season, which I did on a few occasions, you don't usually get much time to work with your players before your first game. Jumping straight in and going straight to the heart of a two-day preparation for a game, like Pochettino has done before United go to Anfield, is so difficult and I am not sure any manager can honestly make a profound difference. A change of voice helps, I'm sure, but so does showing strength and confidence in your own principles and making sure the players understand you demand complete and utter commitment in all the games you face, starting with this one. With time on the training ground being so limited, my initial work would focus on us being a team and working up and down the pitch together, by breaking down different scenarios inside the game and what we should do in them. I'd keep the focus on hard work and making us difficult to beat - clean sheets are so under-rated. Then, on the day, your first pre-match speech is always a massive one, and it will be the same for Pochettino too. My first team talk would always focus on generating an 'us against the world' mentality. As a manager coming in now, you've usually got the job because the team has struggled, so you can play on that to motivate the players. You can use media reports and stories to show the negativity against them - but then counter that by producing a real 'stand-up and be counted' kind of rallying call, before sending them out on the pitch, while mentioning your faith in them to succeed. Pochettino had his first training session with United's players on Thursday [Getty Images] 'What your own eyes tell you is most important' I would have selected my team before I met the players, through my own knowledge and also with help from within. Whichever club I went in at, I'd expect to know something about most of the players within the group in terms of their position and ability, but understanding the character of the squad was vital too. The existing staff would know more about the lads' qualities in that respect than myself or anyone who had just arrived with me, so I'd always discuss that with the people I had inherited, from fitness coaches to the medical department. It's what your own eyes tell you that is most important, however. Going into your first game gives you the opportunity to see for yourself what your players are made of - and it can be a completely different view from what other people see. Most of the early games I managed would be hit and miss in terms of selection, but I would quickly work out the strengths and weaknesses of the group. As I've mentioned in previous columns, one of my first aims at any club where I was manager was about putting out a team, not a group of individuals. It does not take long to see when that is not happening. I can remember my first game of my first spell at Stoke, a 4-2 defeat at Walsall in the Championship. I wasn't universally enamoured by certain crowd favourites in that team and, while any manager knows that leaving some of them out could have an adverse effect on the supporters' view of yourself, you have to stand up and make decisions based on what you see. It is the same if there are other issues with the squad you have inherited too. West Brom's first game after I was appointed manager was a draw with West Ham on New Year's Day 2015. I sat in the stands at Upton Park with my son, Anthony, who was concerned how different the Albion team was compared to Crystal Palace, the last team I had managed in the Premier League. He was right to worry about it, but we still found a way - a totally different way of playing, but still a way to win that suited the group. Pulis (far right) watched West Brom play West Ham with (right to left) his son Anthony, his assistant Dave Kemp and the Baggies' technical director, Terry Burton [Getty Images] All your staff have to understand your objectives My initial aims after arriving at any club mid-season were pretty direct and also pretty basic too. The staff I inherited did not just know the players, they were also the first group who had to understand my objectives and also my principles - like the work ethic I expected, for example. Irrespective of what they were used to doing, it was imperative they followed my lead. One of the clubs I arrived at were struggling at the foot of the table and also suffering from a glut of injuries. In my opinion, the players were taking advantage of a very honest and hard-working medical department, who were quite accommodating on the treatment times for the lads. I changed that immediately, so injured players were treated at 9am, 2pm and 4pm, with sessions in-between those times for strength and recovery workouts. This did not go down well with the players because it impeded on their social lives and, in one case, a player whose injury record was not exactly brilliant came to me complaining that his wife expected him to pick his children up from school and being asked to be in at 4pm affected his private life too. I did not budge, and funnily enough the player in question recovered quite quickly - as did the majority of the other injured players. 'Clear the treatment rooms, and make sure the players are fit' Pulis at work on the training ground with West Brom in 2015 [Getty Images] Asking injured players to be at the training ground all day was by far the best way of getting them fit, in my experience, and the medical departments I managed were all working well past 4pm anyway so it was no hardship to them. Just on that side of things, I would sometimes get the feeling some medical departments thought that, if they weren't treating players, then they weren't doing their jobs. That was completely the opposite to how I saw it. I would congratulate people for having empty treatment rooms and applaud them for their work. Treatment rooms are comfort areas that certain players would always gravitate to, to have a kiss and a cuddle if they are feeling sorry for themselves for not being in the team. That's one of the first things that has to change, because you cannot give your players any excuses or hiding places if they are not performing. Similarly, I have always laughed at new managers who take over in mid-season and complain about the lack of fitness in their squad. I am sure I have done it myself at some point, but then I had a reputation of managing extremely fit squads of players and it was always an area I studied really closely. Early on in my management career, we weren't blessed with the advanced fitness equipment used in football today, but I was still able to quickly arrive at the level I believed the players should be at. How? Simple. Firstly, I had my own fitness runs that were tried and tested but, also, I knew that if during a fitness session they weren't moaning and sweating, they weren't working hard enough. Privately, you can realise very quickly when and which additions to the squad are needed. Pochettino will no doubt be thinking about that at United already, but he has 10 games in the Premier League and Champions League before the January transfer window opens. In the meantime, everything has to be geared towards winning games. I always knew I needed to do that quickly, because it helps the players believe in what I was doing, which is important too. I've outlined my principles I held at every club above, and they never changed, but my playing principles were determined by the quality of the group I inherited. M

item.title: Davis Schneider Issues Statement After Blue Jays Non-Tender Him
item.description: Davis Schneider Blue Jays Getty Former Toronto Blue Jays second baseman and outfielder Davis Schneider issued a statement after he was non-tendered by the team. The Blue Jays non-tendered Schneider on Friday, sending him to free agency immediately after parts of four seasons with the club. Now, he has spoken out following his release. Davis Schneider Grateful to Blue Jays Speaking to Canadian baseball writer Danny Gallagher, Schneider shared his first comments since the Blue Jays released him. “I was kind of expecting it. I knew it might happen. It’s part of the business. It’s part of the game. I’m not going to grind about it too much. It’s one of those things. Life goes on,” Schneider said. “I spent 9½ years with the organization. Toronto is one of the greatest cities I could play for, in the whole country, in all of North America. It’s such a great fan base that wants you to succeed. Toronto fans are the best in the world.” In an exclusive interview with non-tendered Davis Schneider, he told me: "I was kind of expecting it. I knew it might happen. It's part of the business. It's part of the game. I'm not going to grind about it too much. It's one of those things. Life goes on.'' — Danny Gallagher (@dannogallagher7) November 21, 2026 (2) More Davis Schneider: "I spent 9½ years with the organization. Toronto is one of the greatest cities I could play for, in the whole country, in all of North America. It's such a great fan base that wants you to succeed. Toronto fans are the best in the world.'' — Danny Gallagher (@dannogallagher7) November 21, 2026 Where Will Davis Schneider Play Next? The Blue Jays non-tendered Schneider because they did not want to pay his arbitration projection of $1.3 million next year. However, that doesn’t mean that his team in MLB is over, as another team could sign him for something less than that. Teams like the Los Angeles Angels and Colorado Rockies, who need an influx of talent at pretty much every position, should be the first ones to call up Schneider’s agent and see if he would be interested in signing with them, either on a cheap major-league deal, or on a minor-league deal with an invitation to spring training next season. Schneider has some pop in his bat, and he can play left field and second base, so he provides some versatility for whatever team he is on. He is also a great teammate and a fan favorite, so there are a lot of positives to signing him. It’s unfortunate that his time in Toronto ended, but with the Blue Jays looking to improve their roster after missing the playoffs, they had to make some tough decisions, and that meant not tendering Schneider a new contract. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Davis Schneider Issues Statement After Blue Jays Non-Tender Him appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: 'Goosebumps!' - Super-sub Carlos Espi salutes Bernabeu roar after bailing out Real Madrid against Celta
item.description: Real Madrid v RC Celta de Vigo - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Carlos Espi admitted the Santiago Bernabeu atmosphere gave him "goosebumps" after his 85th-minute rebound secured Real Madrid's 2-1 comeback win over Celta Vigo. The young striker stressed squad unity as Los Blancos extended their winning streak to nine matches ahead of Tuesday's Champions League battle. Espi completes late Bernabeu comeback Carlos Espi struck in the 85th minute to seal a 2-1 comeback victory for Real Madrid against Celta Vigo and extend their winning run to nine consecutive matches. After Pablo Duran gave Celta a sixth-minute lead and Kylian Mbappe blazed a first-half penalty over the crossbar, Jude Bellingham levelled on 66 minutes before Espi pounced on a rebound from Vinicius Junior's cross. The decisive finish marked the Valencian forward's fourth goal of the campaign and preserved Real Madrid's perfect home record this season. Speaking after the final whistle, Espi admitted the backing from the stands left a powerful impression on him. Match-winner reveals 'goosebumps' from crowd support Espi explained that every substitute entered the pitch determined to turn the contest around , crediting the collective spirit inside the 23-to-24-man squad alongside the vocal home crowd. "I get goosebumps," Espi said. "It's indescribable how much support I feel from everyone. I will give my all for the madridistas and for this club. I try to do what the coach asks of me, and every minute I get, I will make the most of it. If I can help the team, even better. As I said the other day, the goal is to stay united. We're 23-24 players, and we all need to move in the same direction. Those of us who came on did so fully focused on securing the victory, and that's what we achieved." Home fortress fuels ninth straight triumph While Real Madrid endured a frustrating opening half, Espi insisted dropping points at the Santiago Bernabeu was never an option once the crowd lifted the team in the second period. "Honestly, the fans are incredible; they support us from the very first minute," he added. "Today, they carried us forward. We can't afford to drop points here. Honestly, it's a real energy boost. It was a tough match that we managed to win, and now we have to keep moving forward because this doesn't stop—there's another battle in the Champions League." Full focus shifts to Tuesday's Champions League tie With only 48 hours to recover from a demanding domestic test, Espi stressed that Los Blancos must immediately channel their momentum into European action. "Now, the most important thing is Tuesday because this doesn't stop," he concluded. "We have two days to prepare for the match, and with all our enthusiasm, we're going for it."

item.title: Bucks’ Tyler Herro Makes NBA History Despite 13-Game Losing Streak
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 21: Tyler Herro #11 of the Milwaukee Bucks in action during a game against the Philadelphia 76ers at Xfinity Mobile Arena on November 21, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 21: Tyler Herro #11 of the Milwaukee Bucks drives against Dominick Barlow #25 of the Philadelphia 76ers during the first half of a game at Xfinity Mobile Arena on November 21, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) Getty The Milwaukee Bucks have spent much of November searching for a win. At least, Tyler Herro gave them a performance for the NBA record books. Herro scored a career-high 50 points against Philadelphia on Nov. 21. He added 11 rebounds and seven assists, carrying Milwaukee within one shot of overtime. The Bucks lost 132-129. But the team highlighted a piece of league history that belonged to its guard alone. In its announcement on X , Milwaukee called Herro the “first player in NBA history” to reach four statistical thresholds together. Tyler Herro is the first player in NBA history to have 50+ PTS, 11+ REB, 7+ 3PM, and 65% FG in a single game. pic.twitter.com/8PTq15qp53 — Milwaukee Bucks (@Bucks) November 21, 2026 Bucks Announce Tyler Herro’s Historic Stat Line Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – NOVEMBER 21: Tyler Herro #11 of the Milwaukee Bucks drives against Dominick Barlow #25 of the Philadelphia 76ers during the first half of a game at Xfinity Mobile Arena on November 21, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) The Bucks said Herro became the first player in NBA history with at least 50 points, 11 rebounds and seven made 3-pointers while shooting at least 65% from the field in a single game. That distinction covers all four marks together. It does not mean Herro became the first player to record 50 points and 11 rebounds. His efficiency made the scoring total stand out. The game’s box score lists him at 15-for-23 from the floor and 7-for-12 from beyond the arc. Those figures work out to 65.2% overall and 58.3% on 3-pointers. Herro made all 13 free throws, too. He needed only 23 field-goal attempts to reach 50 points, with his trips to the line providing more than a quarter of that total. He contributed in areas other than his shot-making. The guard grabbed three offensive rebounds and eight defensive boards, handed out seven assists and committed two turnovers in nearly 40 minutes. The outburst followed a rough stretch. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 21: Tyler Herro #11 of the Milwaukee Bucks drives against Dominick Barlow #25 of the Philadelphia 76ers during the first half of a game at Xfinity Mobile Arena on November 21, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) Getty The Milwaukee Bucks have spent much of November searching for a win. At least, Tyler Herro gave them a performance for the NBA record books. Herro scored a career-high 50 points against Philadelphia on Nov. 21. He added 11 rebounds and seven assists, carrying Milwaukee within one shot of overtime. The Bucks lost 132-129. But the team highlighted a piece of league history that belonged to its guard alone. In its announcement on X , Milwaukee called Herro the “first player in NBA history” to reach four statistical thresholds together. Tyler Herro is the first player in NBA history to have 50+ PTS, 11+ REB, 7+ 3PM, and 65% FG in a single game. pic.twitter.com/8PTq15qp53 — Milwaukee Bucks (@Bucks) November 21, 2026 Bucks Announce Tyler Herro’s Historic Stat Line Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – NOVEMBER 21: Tyler Herro #11 of the Milwaukee Bucks drives against Dominick Barlow #25 of the Philadelphia 76ers during the first half of a game at Xfinity Mobile Arena on November 21, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) The Bucks said Herro became the first player in NBA history with at least 50 points, 11 rebounds and seven made 3-pointers while shooting at least 65% from the field in a single game. That distinction covers all four marks together. It does not mean Herro became the first player to record 50 points and 11 rebounds. His efficiency made the scoring total stand out. The game’s box score lists him at 15-for-23 from the floor and 7-for-12 from beyond the arc. Those figures work out to 65.2% overall and 58.3% on 3-pointers. Herro made all 13 free throws, too. He needed only 23 field-goal attempts to reach 50 points, with his trips to the line providing more than a quarter of that total. He contributed in areas other than his shot-making. The guard grabbed three offensive rebounds and eight defensive boards, handed out seven assists and committed two turnovers in nearly 40 minutes. The outburst followed a rough stretch. The NBA’s game log shows Herro scored 18, five, eight and 19 points in his previous four appearances. He matched that combined total against the 76ers. Herro’s Final Shot Arrives Too Late for Bucks Milwaukee nearly turned the milestone into a comeback win. As Field Level Media reported via Reuters , Philadelphia led by 10 with just over two minutes remaining. Herro helped cut the deficit before Brayden Burries hit a 3-pointer with 4.8 seconds left. Two Philadelphia free throws left Milwaukee trailing by three. With 1.5 seconds remaining, the Bucks found Herro on the inbound pass. His shot went in, but replay showed the ball remained on his fingertips when time expired. The reversal left him at 50 points and sent Milwaukee home with another loss. The result dropped the Bucks to 1-16 and extended their losing streak to 13 games, according to the Associated Press game report . The shooting for Herro marked a sharp difference from his recent outings. He went a combined 0-for-10 from deep against Atlanta and Miami, then made four of seven against Portland. He carried that improved touch into Philadelphia. Milwaukee needs that production to last for many afternoons. Herro supplied points, rebounds and passing against the 76ers, and the team still finished one possession short. His final basket could have bought five more minutes. Instead, the Bucks left with a record-setting performance and the same losing streak. item.title: 14-year-old Adrian Peterson Jr. receives offer from Oklahoma
item.description: BRYAN TERRY/THE OKLAHOMAN / USA TODAY NETWORK 14-year-old Adrian Peterson Jr. receives offer from Oklahoma appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Oklahoma has extended a scholarship offer to Adrian Peterson Jr., giving the son of former Sooners standout and NFL running back Adrian Peterson an opportunity to follow in his father’s footsteps in Norman. The 14-year-old announced Saturday on social media that he received an offer from the Sooners. A member of the 2030 recruiting class, Peterson Jr. is currently a freshman at Fort Bend Ridge Point High School in Missouri City, Texas. He is listed at 6-foot-1 and 175 pounds and has experience playing multiple positions, including running back, wide receiver and defensive back. Peterson Jr. has already attracted considerable attention from college programs. His scholarship offers include Miami, Florida State, Texas Tech, Texas A&M, Baylor, Minnesota, Syracuse, TCU, SMU, UTSA, Missouri State and Texas State, along with Oklahoma, according to 247Sports. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The young athlete has begun making an impact at the high school level. Through six games, he has recorded seven receptions for 95 yards and two touchdowns, according to MaxPreps. His father became one of the Sooners’ most accomplished players between 2004 and 2006. Adrian Peterson Sr. racked up 4,041 rushing yards and 41 touchdowns across three seasons with the Sooners, averaging 5.4 yards per carry. He was a unanimous All-American in 2004, finished as the Heisman Trophy runner-up and earned first-team All-Big 12 recognition in each of his three seasons. Peterson Sr. eventually carried that success into the NFL, finishing his 15-year professional career with 14,918 rushing yards, the fifth-highest total among running backs in league history. With Oklahoma now among the programs pursuing his son, the Sooners have an opportunity to add another member of the Peterson family to their football program when the 2030 recruiting cycle arrives. item.title: Maple Leafs Need to Fire Jim Hiller After Latest Collapse
item.description: Jim Hiller Maple Leafs Getty The time has come for the Toronto Maple Leafs to grow some stones and fire head coach Jim Hiller. This statement isn’t some knee-jerk reaction to the team’s most recent loss. It’s a natural consequence of yet another third-period collapse. The Maple Leafs were leading 3-1 midway through the second period before three unanswered goals led to a Columbus Blue Jackets’ 4-3 win. But it was the two goals roughly a minute apart that added insult to injury. Sure, Hiller wasn’t on the ice for the two goals. He wasn’t playing in goal. He wasn’t the guy who didn’t block a shot or clear the puck from the zone. However, someone has to be accountable for the situation. Someone has to answer to the latest debacle. And as much as the players are to blame for the situation, the bottom line is that the ax has to fall somewhere, and that somewhere will be Jim Hiller’s head. Do the Maple Leafs Have Any Other Choice? While it’s easy to call for the coach’s head, the fact of the matter is: Do the Maple Leafs have any other choice? Does the organization have any other realistic path forward? Hiller doesn’t seem to have an answer for any of what’s going on. He doesn’t seem to grasp the seriousness of the situation befalling the team. Meanwhile, GM John Chayka is feeling the heat. He’s the guy responsible for hiring Hiller. That’s why one has to think that there is no other way around this. Chayka can either fess up to his mistake and try to right the wrong, or stubbornly try to wiggle his way out of the mess. It’s clear that he’s out of runway. The Maple Leafs are in a death spiral with no clear end in sight. Something has to give. Unless there’s a magic solution that no one is aware of, the Leafs don’t really have any other choice. The chain will have to break in the weakest link, and that link is Jim Hiller. Any Option Is Better Than Nothing at This Point Yes, it’s true that no move is better than a bad move. That situation applied to the Leafs a week ago. Now, that’s not the case anymore. While the goal is not to make a gut-call at this time, the fact is that something will have to change. The Maple Leafs cannot afford to let this latest mess go unanswered. It will either have to be a massive trade to really shake the team up, or it will have to be a coaching change. The latter is the easiest way out for now. It’s also worth noting that a coaching change won’t preclude a trade. Nevertheless, Chayka can’t tip his hand right now. Everyone knows he’s in a bind. So, there won’t be any compassion from any other GM out there. Let’s see what happens. The Maple Leafs next game will be on Monday night in Long Island against the Islanders. That gives the organization very little time to make a decision, if any. Regardless of the tight turnaround, there may be no other way out. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Maple Leafs Need to Fire Jim Hiller After Latest Collapse appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Yahoo Top 10: Wild Week 12 shakes up college football rankings
item.description: The most mundane weekends in college football can often turn into mayhem. Two of the Big Ten's best playoff challengers (UCLA and Indiana) lost, preseason No. 1 Ohio State took a fourth 'L' this season and LSU — its high-priced head coach, Lane Kiffin, and $40 million-plus roster — dropped a fifth game. The Bruins and Hoosiers served up the biggest surprises with overtime losses at Michigan and Washington, respectively, tossing the conference into a bit of chaos and uncertainty. Can the Big Ten win a fourth straight national championship ? At this point, the odds seem steep for even getting more than two teams into the playoff. Also in the conference, Ohio State became the first preseason top-ranked team to lose at least four games since USC in 2012 as the Buckeyes dropped a game at Nebraska. In the SEC, Tennessee kept its playoff hopes alive with a throttling of LSU in Knoxville, and Georgia survived the always-scary trip to Columbia, South Carolina. The Big 12 race is Utah, BYU and Texas Tech. Meanwhile, Miami and Wake Forest are on a collision course for a rematch in Charlotte (the Hurricanes won Round 1, 33-20) for all the ACC marbles. 1. Utah Utes This week: beat TCU 38-17 Next week: vs. West Virginia The Utes blew open a 17-17 tie with three consecutive touchdowns in the final six minutes of the game. QB Devon Dampier scored the last two TDs — one passing and another rushing — on a night when he led the team on the ground and through the air. Dampier had more than 325 total yards and Larry Simmons caught three passes for a whopping 114 yards as Utah clinched a Big 12 championship game appearance. 2. Georgia Bulldogs This week: beat South Carolina 34-6 Next week: vs. Georgia Tech Is anyone playing better football than Kirby Smart’s crew? Smart's team turned a tight game into a blowout in the second half, even recovering a surprise onside kick in the third quarter. Gunner Stockton continues to be one of the nation's leaders in efficiency (19 of 23) and the Bulldogs know how to run the ball (Nate Frazier had 94 yards). But DC Glenn Schumann's defensive unit was great from the start in Columbia on Saturday night. Ethan Barbour and the Georgia Bulldogs have plenty of reasons to flex these days. Icon Sportswire via Getty Images 3. Notre Dame Fighting Irish This week: beat SMU 24-3 Next week: at Syracuse After beating Miami and bludgeoning SMU, there is little argument that the Irish, with a season-ending win over Syracuse next week, will make the 12-team postseason. The loss to BYU stings, sure, but Notre Dame QB CJ Carr continues to be one of the biggest challengers in the Heisman Trophy race. He threw for more than 300 yards against the Mustangs. 4. Georgia Bulldogs This week: beat South Carolina 34-6 Next week: vs. Georgia Tech Is anyone playing better football than Kirby Smart’s crew? Smart's team turned a tight game into a blowout in the second half, even recovering a surprise onside kick in the third quarter. Icon Sportswire via Getty Images 3. Notre Dame Fighting Irish This week: beat SMU 24-3 Next week: at Syracuse After beating Miami and bludgeoning SMU, there is little argument that the Irish, with a season-ending win over Syracuse next week, will make the 12-team postseason. The loss to BYU stings, sure, but Notre Dame QB CJ Carr continues to be one of the biggest challengers in the Heisman Trophy race. He threw for more than 300 yards against the Mustangs. 4. Miami Hurricanes This week: beat Virginia Tech 28-20 Next week: vs. Boston College Down 14-0? No problem. The Hurricanes mounted a comeback at Hard Rock Stadium to solidify a trip to Charlotte for the ACC championship game — despite QB Darian Mensah not throwing a single touchdown pass. In fact, he had two interceptions to match his season total to this point. But Miami's defense rose to the challenge after the early hole, forcing Tech into five punts on its next seven drives. 5. Wake Forest Demon Deacons This week: beat Georgia Tech 50-29 Next week: vs. Duke If there was still any doubt that the Demon Deacons are real playoff challengers, those should be put to bed. Jake Dickert's team has outscored its last seven opponents 363-67. QB Gio Lopez threw for two touchdowns and ran for two more in the shellacking of the Yellow Jackets. Wake is barreling toward an ACC championship game appearance and a playoff spot. 6. Alabama Crimson Tide This week: beat Chattanooga 47-0 Next week: vs. Auburn The Tide rested Keelon Russell, and why not? The 7-5 FCS Mocs didn't stand a chance. Seven of Chattanooga's 10 drives lasted three plays or less. Kane Wommack, a candidate for several head coaching gigs, and his defensive unit has allowed 20 points the last three games. Bama is headed to the playoff with a win in the Iron Bowl. 7. UCLA Bruins This week: lost to Michigan 18-16 (3OT) Next week: vs. USC Michigan QB Bryce Underwood completed just 11 passes and was sacked four times. And while that doesn't sound like the stat line of a winner, the Bruins offense couldn't muster enough to beat the Wolverines. Ty Dieffenbach was sacked four times, threw an interception and lost a costly fumble that set up Michigan for the go-ahead score. 8. Texas Longhorns This week: beat Arkansas 45-3 Next week: vs. Texas A&M Arch Manning had four incompletions and three touchdowns in the win over the lowly Razorbacks. There's no hiding the Longhorns' deficiencies, but Texas has the talent to win it all and a victory over the Aggies next week will send them to the 12-team playoff. After back-to-back losses to Florida and Oklahoma, the Horns have won five straight. 9. Iowa Hawkeyes This week: beat Illinois 34-17 Next week: vs. Nebraska No one benefitted from Saturday's Big Ten upset bonanza quite like the Hawkeyes. They are now in striking distance to advance to the playoff. And who would want to play Phil Parker's defense and an offensive unit that moves the ball better than any Hawkeye version in years. Iowa shut out the Illini in the second half and backup RB L.J. Phillips, in for the injured Kamari Moulton, ran for 154 yards — this third straight 100-yard outing. 10. Tennessee Volunteers This week: beat LSU 27-13 Next week: at Vanderbilt When in doubt, run QB Faizon Brandon. That's what the Vols did. He ran for 112 yards on just 12 carries — nearly 10 yards a pop — and scored two touchdowns in the fourth quarter. It was more than enough for Tennessee to re-enter our Top 10 ahead of a big game in Nashville next week. Win and they're (likely) in the postseason.

item.title: No. 17 Boise State suffers costly loss to San Diego State after late clock-management snafu
item.description: San Diego State defenders celebrate after recovering a fumble by Boise State quarterback Maddux Madsen on Saturday in Boise, Idaho. AP Photo/Darin Oswald San Diego State hit a field goal as time expired to beat No. 17 Boise State 22-20 in a stunning upset Saturday night on Boise's famed blue turf. Cooper DiLeva's winning 42-yard kick deals a serious blow to Boise's College Football Playoff hopes, which it could earn by finishing the season as the highest-ranked Group of Six team. The Broncos (9-2) are by no means out of playoff contention, and will still play for the Pac-12 title in two weeks, but the loss opens the door for another G6 contender. BALL. GAME. San Diego State will be back at Boise in two weeks to compete for a Pac-12 Championship 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LE2aLr97sy — USA Sports (@usasports) November 22, 2026 SDSU's victory was made possible by a bizarre sequence in the final minutes as the Broncos were trying to run out the clock with the ball. On third-and-8 with 1:41 on the clock, BSU threw a pass that ended up with tight end Keawe Browne out of bounds, which stopped the clock at 1:36. The Aztecs had zero timeouts so that was a huge favor. On the next play, fourth-and-3 at the SDSU 45-yard line, BSU tried for the first down rather than punting and pinning back the Aztecs. Quarterback Maddux Madsen was stuffed for a loss, giving SDSU the ball in prime field position with 1:31 left on the clock. The Aztecs (6-5) quickly drove into field-goal range to set up the winning kick. SDSU QB Stone Saunders played a part in both of his team's touchdowns, scoring on a 9-yard run in the third quarter and throwing a 39-yard scoring pass to Jaylon Hawkins with 1:58 to play. San Diego could have tied it with a PAT at that point but opted to go for 2 and came up short. That gave Boise State the ball with a 20-19 lead and under two minutes to play, but the Broncos weren't able to close out the victory.

item.title: Live: Finland says war 'spilling over' after Baltic Sea drone strike on Russian cargo ship
item.description: Finland warned the war in Ukraine was "spilling over" after a drone set ablaze a Russian cargo ship on the eastern Baltic Sea on Saturday. Helsinki stressed that Kyiv had the right to defend itself against Moscow's aggression. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

item.title: Ekiti govt disowns purported climate action award
item.description: The Ekiti State Government has dissociated itself, Governor Biodun Oyebanji and his administration from a purported Best African Governor for Climate Action Award reportedly presented to the Governor. According to a publication, the award was presented by the King’s College African Leadership Centre at its inaugural Climate Action Awards ceremony, held on the sidelines of COP 31 in Antalya, Türkiye, in collaboration with the Ondo State Oil Producing Areas Development Commission (OSOPADEC). The Government, however, wishes to state categorically that Governor Oyebanji was neither aware of the purported award nor involved in its presentation. He did not attend the ceremony, nor authorise anyone to receive it on his behalf. This disclaimer has become necessary to set the record straight and prevent members of the public from being misled by claims that are not only false but could also be part of a dubious publicity stunt. Governor Oyebanji’s administration is guided by the principles of accountability, transparency and integrity. While the Governor has received several recognitions and awards from credible organisations and reputable institutions in acknowledgement of his contributions to governance and development, the Governor does not endorse or associate himself with questionable awards from organisations whose credibility and intentions are unclear. Members of the public and the media are therefore urged to disregard the report and treat the purported award as unauthorised and unrecognised by the Governor and the Ekiti State Government. item.content:encoded: The Ekiti State Government has dissociated itself, Governor Biodun Oyebanji and his administration from a purported Best African Governor for Climate Action Award reportedly presented to the Governor. According to a publication, the award was presented by the King’s College African Leadership Centre at its inaugural Climate Action Awards ceremony, held on the sidelines of COP 31 in Antalya, Türkiye, in collaboration with the Ondo State Oil Producing Areas Development Commission (OSOPADEC). The Government, however, wishes to state categorically that Governor Oyebanji was neither aware of the purported award nor involved in its presentation. He did not attend the ceremony, nor authorise anyone to receive it on his behalf. This disclaimer has become necessary to set the record straight and prevent members of the public from being misled by claims that are not only false but could also be part of a dubious publicity stunt. Governor Oyebanji’s administration is guided by the principles of accountability, transparency and integrity. While the Governor has received several recognitions and awards from credible organisations and reputable institutions in acknowledgement of his contributions to governance and development, the Governor does not endorse or associate himself with questionable awards from organisations whose credibility and intentions are unclear. item.title: Otti disowns viral statement against campaign rallies, calls it fake
item.description: By Steve Oko Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has disowned a viral social media statement purportedly credited to him, describing it as fake and warning the public against spreading misinformation. The statement, which circulated on X (formerly Twitter), quoted Otti as saying that incumbent governors who embark on campaigns have no business doing so if they have performed well, arguing that their achievements should speak for them and secure their re-election. It also quoted the governor as saying he was not campaigning and that Abia residents should re-elect him only if they considered his performance satisfactory. However, the governor, through his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Ferdinand Ekeoma, on Friday, dismissed the statement and the X account that published it as fake. Ekeoma, who signed the disclaimer, said Otti never made the statement and urged the public not to be misled by the publication. He explained that, contrary to the impression created by the viral post, the governor was already campaigning and had been touring different parts of the state to interact with voters and obtain firsthand feedback, particularly from grassroots communities. According to him, Otti considers campaigns a legitimate component of the electoral process and could not have disparaged politicians for engaging in them. “The Governor believes that campaigns are legitimate parts of the electoral process and thus could not have dismissed it or cast aspersions on those campaigning,” Ekeoma said. The state government urged members of the public to disregard the purported statement and the account responsible for circulating it, while calling on those behind the publication to immediately take it down and desist from misrepresenting the governor. It also cautioned individuals using Otti’s popularity to generate online traffic to ensure that information published in his name is truthful, warning that deliberate misrepresentation could attract the attention of law enforcement agencies. The disclaimer comes amid growing political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, with social media increasingly serving as a platform for political messaging, claims and counterclaims. Meanwhile, Vanguard investigations indicate that Otti currently faces no formidable challenger in the forthcoming governorship election. The post Otti disowns viral statement against campaign rallies, calls it fake appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘Serious error of judgment’: outrage over military AI event at Berlin arts complex
item.description: Kraftwerk Berlin, part of same development as techno club Tresor, transformed into ‘war room’ for arms firm event With their cavernous post-industrial venues, teeth-grinding four-by-four beats and bouncers that look like Blade Runner extras, Berlin’s nightclubs trade on a reputation for bleakness. A recent event at one of the city’s most legendary clubland institutions, however, has proven too dystopian even for seasoned techno-heads. On 11 November, the Kraftwerk Berlin arts complex had its central hall transformed into what visitors described as something resembling a war room, with maps and aerial footage projected on to concrete walls, drones hanging from the ceiling, and guards in flak jackets patrolling the premises with sniffer dogs. Continue reading...

item.title: Hacks, AI and conspiracy theories: why are we having so many outages?
item.description: After chaos at airlines, banks and companies from Microsoft to Apple, people have become convinced the world’s systems are under attack Nicole Reindorf’s American Airlines flight was ready for takeoff in Phoenix when the pilot came on the intercom and announced what was to become the longest nationwide aviation shutdown since 9/11 . Reindorf, 70, had seen the headlines hours before about a global Microsoft outage . She immediately suspected the two were linked in some way by AI-related threats – and that she would not get to the wedding of her best friend’s son in California. Continue reading...

item.title: 2027: Who speaks for the North as ACF crisis deepens?
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo As the 2027 general elections draw closer, an increasingly important question is emerging in Northern Nigeria: Who speaks for the North, and whose position represents the collective interests of the region? The question has assumed greater significance amid the lingering leadership crisis in the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF), one of the North’s longstanding socio-political platforms, and growing disagreements among prominent Northern politicians, elder statesmen and interest groups over the direction the region should take in the next general elections. For decades, the ACF provided an important platform for articulating Northern interests, engaging governments and promoting regional cohesion. However, its current internal disagreements, involving its Board of Trustees and National Executive Committee, have raised questions about its ability to provide the kind of unified regional leadership expected of it at a critical political moment. The dispute has reportedly degenerated into competing claims of authority, allegations of constitutional breaches and disagreements over the management of the organisation’s affairs. The development may create an opening for other political and socio-cultural platforms to occupy the space traditionally associated with the ACF. Indeed, the struggle over who represents Northern opinion became more apparent on Wednesday when the Arewa Emerging Elites Round Table challenged some prominent Northern figures over their criticism of President Bola Tinubu’s administration. item.dc:creator: Oboh
item.content:encoded: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo As the 2027 general elections draw closer, an increasingly important question is emerging in Northern Nigeria: Who speaks for the North, and whose position represents the collective interests of the region? The question has assumed greater significance amid the lingering leadership crisis in the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF), one of the North’s longstanding socio-political platforms, and growing disagreements among prominent Northern politicians, elder statesmen and interest groups over the direction the region should take in the next general elections. For decades, the ACF provided an important platform for articulating Northern interests, engaging governments and promoting regional cohesion. However, its current internal disagreements, involving its Board of Trustees and National Executive Committee, have raised questions about its ability to provide the kind of unified regional leadership expected of it at a critical political moment. The dispute has reportedly degenerated into competing claims of authority, allegations of constitutional breaches and disagreements over the management of the organisation’s affairs. The development may create an opening for other political and socio-cultural platforms to occupy the space traditionally associated with the ACF. Indeed, the struggle over who represents Northern opinion became more apparent on Wednesday when the Arewa Emerging Elites Round Table challenged some prominent Northern figures over their criticism of President Bola Tinubu’s administration. At a press conference in Kaduna, the group, through its chairman, Abubakar A. Kurawa, faulted Dr Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, Dr Usman Bugaje, former Minister Adamu Maina Waziri and former National Health Insurance Scheme Executive Secretary, Prof Usman Yusuf, for what it described as presenting partisan political positions as the collective position of Northern Nigeria. In a briefing titled, Stop Hiding Naked Partisanship Behind the Sacred Robes of Arewa Eldership: You Do Not Speak for the North!, the organisation questioned the mandate under which the four personalities purportedly spoke for the region. It argued that neither previous public offices nor political prominence automatically conferred the authority to determine the political direction of the 19 Northern states. The group particularly questioned whether traditional rulers, religious leaders, youth organisations, professional associations, farmers, traders and ordinary citizens had been adequately consulted before positions were presented as representing the North. It also challenged the former public office holders to demonstrate their contributions to regional development, insisting that discussions about Northern leadership should go beyond political rhetoric to measurable achievements. Meanwhile, Murtala Mohammed, an Kaduna based critic, said the intervention has also brought another dimension to the debate: Whether those challenging the authority of established Northern voices are themselves speaking from a sufficiently broad regional mandate. “The argument is significant because the four personalities criticised by the group are entitled, like other Nigerians, to express their political opinions and question government policies”, he said. “The more important distinction is between expressing personal or partisan positions and claiming to represent an entire region.” Political realignments The controversy comes against the background of increasing political realignments ahead of 2027. While some Northern politicians and groups have expressed reservations about the Tinubu administration, others are advocating continuity and greater engagement with the Federal Government. At the Kaduna Summit on Inclusivity, Good Governance and Sustainable Development organised by the Sir Ahmadu Bello Memorial Foundation on Wednesday, former Niger State Governor, Mu’azu Babangida Aliyu, endorsed Governor Uba Sani for a second term, citing his administration’s record in security, education, healthcare, agriculture and infrastructure. The foundation’s Director-General, Abubakar Gambo Umar, also highlighted the importance of continuity and inclusive governance. Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, represented by Deputy Speaker Ado Doguwa, called for accountability and constructive criticism while acknowledging continuing security challenges, particularly in Southern Kaduna. Governor Uba Sani, however, went beyond the immediate Kaduna political debate, urging the foundation to mobilise Northern leaders towards developing a comprehensive regional development agenda. He recalled the vision of the late Premier of Northern Nigeria, Sir Ahmadu Bello, for a united, peaceful and self-sufficient North, arguing that subsequent generations of leaders had departed from that vision. His call raises an important question: Can Northern leaders agree on a common development agenda despite their differences over political parties, presidential succession and the 2027 elections? Platforms There are also other emerging platforms. The League of Northern Democrats, led by former Kano State Governor Ibrahim Shekarau, has been engaging the ACF, Northern Elders Forum and Middle Belt Forum on the possibility of building a common front around the region’s challenges. Yet, the existence of several organisations does not necessarily translate into a coherent regional voice. “The North’s problems extend beyond political representation. Insecurity, poverty, unemployment, educational backwardness, agricultural difficulties, infrastructure deficits and economic hardship require sustained engagement and measurable interventions,” said Murtala. “Consequently, the question of who speaks for the North should not be reduced to who supports or opposes Tinubu, who wants power returned to the region or which political camp commands the loudest following. “Neither should the North be treated as a politically homogeneous constituency whose millions of people must necessarily subscribe to one political position”. The ACF crisis therefore presents an opportunity for serious introspection. Its founding mission of promoting Northern unity and socio-economic advancement remains relevant, but rebuilding confidence in the organisation requires resolving its internal disagreements and restoring its institutional credibility. Similarly, emerging Arewa groups must demonstrate inclusiveness, independence and accountability rather than simply becoming competing platforms for political interests. Ultimately, Northern leadership ahead of 2027 should be measured not by the ability to mobilise endorsements, issue press statements or condemn political opponents, but by the capacity to develop a common agenda, build consensus across regional divides and hold governments accountable. ACF speaks Reacting, the National Publicity Secretary of the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF), Prof. Tukur Muhammad Baba, told Sunday Vanguard that differences of opinion within the forum were natural and should not be mistaken for a breakdown of unity or purpose. He said such differences did not detract from the forum’s commitment to consultation, constructive engagement and advocacy on issues of common interest, including good governance in all its ramifications. He explained that the ACF remained committed to holding elected officials accountable, promoting the fight against corruption and advocating policies that would advance the welfare of the people. Baba noted that the forum had consistently called on governments at all levels to intensify efforts to tackle insecurity, stressing that it had never relented in demanding decisive action against the persistent security challenges confronting the North. Pundits argue that the North does not necessarily need one political voice, but needs credible institutions capable of accommodating different voices while agreeing on the fundamental interests of its people. item.title: Why I’m teaming up with progressive allies in Oyo for Tinubu — Oduyoye, ex-Reps Chief Whip
item.description: By Nnamdi Ojiego Honourable Babatunde Oduyoye was the Chief Whip of the Alliance for Democracy in the House of Representatives where he represented Ibadan Nort-West /South-West Federal Constituency between 1999 and 2007. He had also served as Special Adviser on Political Matters to Governor Seyi Makinde, as well as a member of Oyo State Advisory Council. He is one of the appointees that opened the recent gale of resignations from the government of Oyo State. In this interview, he speaks on why he left Makinde, why he is teaming up with other progressives to support the reelection of President Bola Tinubu and why the progressives need to undertake a rescue mission in Oyo State. Excerpts: Some time ago, you announced your resignation from Oyo State Advisory Council, thus opening the floodgates for the resignations of many others from Governor Seyi Makinde’s government. After the announcement, we didn’t hear much from you. What happened? The Advisory Council is expected to advise the governor on the policy, politics, and administration. As of the time I resigned, I mentioned personal reasons, and it was to improve myself in certain areas. Apart from that, I had a feeling that the council had outlived its usefulness. Once you have a council that is not up and doing, or is doing the proper thing, and the governor is not recognising it, there was no need to sit in that council anymore. That is why, honorably, I resigned. In the resignation letter, you said you had not joined any other party apart from the Alliance for Democracy (AD). And we know that the AD is no longer a registered political party. Can you give us an insight into your political direction going forward? There were times I represented the governor outside the state, specifically in Edo and Kogi States. But there was never a time they called a meeting of leaders of the PDP in the southwestern part that they invited me. item.dc:creator: Oboh
item.content:encoded: By Nnamdi Ojiego Honourable Babatunde Oduyoye was the Chief Whip of the Alliance for Democracy in the House of Representatives where he represented Ibadan Nort-West /South-West Federal Constituency between 1999 and 2007. He had also served as Special Adviser on Political Matters to Governor Seyi Makinde, as well as a member of Oyo State Advisory Council. He is one of the appointees that opened the recent gale of resignations from the government of Oyo State. In this interview, he speaks on why he left Makinde, why he is teaming up with other progressives to support the reelection of President Bola Tinubu and why the progressives need to undertake a rescue mission in Oyo State. Excerpts: Some time ago, you announced your resignation from Oyo State Advisory Council, thus opening the floodgates for the resignations of many others from Governor Seyi Makinde’s government. After the announcement, we didn’t hear much from you. What happened? The Advisory Council is expected to advise the governor on the policy, politics, and administration. As of the time I resigned, I mentioned personal reasons, and it was to improve myself in certain areas. Apart from that, I had a feeling that the council had outlived its usefulness. Once you have a council that is not up and doing, or is doing the proper thing, and the governor is not recognising it, there was no need to sit in that council anymore. That is why, honorably, I resigned. In the resignation letter, you said you had not joined any other party apart from the Alliance for Democracy (AD). And we know that the AD is no longer a registered political party. Can you give us an insight into your political direction going forward? I was, at no point in time, a card-carrying member of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), neither did I attend any local government or state meeting. All my activities within the party were from the purview of my office, first as the Special Adviser on Strategy and Politics to the governor of Oyo State and later as member of Advisory Council. There were times I represented the governor outside the state, specifically in Edo and Kogi States. But there was never a time they called a meeting of leaders of the PDP in the southwestern part that they invited me. There was even a time I sent out an invitation on behalf of the governor for a meeting of the South-West chapter to hold in Ibadan and I remember a commissioner from Osun State then, raised the issue that why was a non-member of the PDP inviting them to a PDP meeting? However, what happened in 2019 was that as members of the AD, we joined hands with Seyi Makinde to assist him, with the likes of Tunde Tijani, Pastor Akinade Akanmu, who later emerged the Chairman of TESCOM and he also joined me in the Advisory Council. What is next, going forward, now that the AD is no more? What should the people of Oyo expect from you after leaving the government of Makinde? Before I left the government of Makinde, my good friend and brother, I have been very close to a brother and friend too, in the person of Oloye Dotun Sanusi, Okanlomo Odua. And this was known to the government, and quite a few people, that we were pushing for him to the governorafter Seyi Makinde, because I believed he has all it takes to govern Oyo State. But the idea was not welcomed in some quarters. And apart from that, he is a very busy man. And it was surprising that an idea that has not even crystalised became toxic in some quarters even before it took off, as some people started ganging up against him. And as a member of the Advisory Council, we were given the responsibility of assisting the government to choose the would-be candidate of the governor’s party. Governor Makinde wanted us, as the Advisory Council, to recommend. And we submitted quite a few names. And top of the list was the retired Commissioner of Police, Fatai Owoseni. The council unanimously endorsed Owoseni. Segun Ogunwuyi,then-Chief of Staff to the governor, came second. And some ofus were pressurizing that Nureni Adeniran should be number three, but the Chairman, Bolaji Ayorinde, and some other people pushed for Bimbo Adekanmbi as number three. Weeks after, we were told that what we recommended was turned upside down. The chairman submitted a report, we as a committee had the responsibility to submit a report. I have read contradictory newspaper reports. But I’m saying authoritatively, as a member who participated in the meetings, that Owoseni was unanimously endorsed by those who were present and by those who joined virtually on Zoom. So that contributed to my resignation from the Advisory Council. Because if we could come in, sit down for almost two days, do something, and at the end of the day, the final decision is that of the governor and our effort did not see the light of the day, that was why I abandoned it. Let me add that some governors are beginning to add things that are strange to the practice of democracy these days. Democracy, as we know, and as it is practiced worldwide, I don’t think it is normal for a sitting governor to announce publicly that he has a preferred candidate. Two governors, the governor of Nasarawa and that of Oyo State brought that up in our political lexicon in the current political situation. For us to get the best in politics, we should provide a level-playing ground for all aspirants to be tested. And at the end of the day, an aspirant who emerges the candidate is bound to have the followership and everybody within thestate will key in to such a thing. But what we have is the reverse. You referred to Governor Makinde as your friend and brother. He is contesting to be president of Nigeria. Will you vote for him? No. And why would that be so? Well, when he wanted to be governor, and he has acknowledged this severally, he came to me, we discussed, and I was convinced. And he said it at my 60th birthday lecture at UI. From the moment I said yes, there was no looking back. There was a time I had an interview with some journalists when it was rumoured that he wanted to be the President of Nigeria, I cautioned then that he knew what to do. And not only that, I believed it was a thing he should discuss or maybe discussed with people close to him, but I was never part of such a discussion. So, why would I key into an agenda that I am unaware of? And the same thing happened to the man he is supporting as governorship candidate. I have never met him. I was not part of the government of the late Senator Abiola Ajimobi. The responsibility and understanding I had with Makinde was for him to be elected as governor of Oyo and for him to do well in office. And it ends there. Your good friend and brother, Dotun Sanusi, has already declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election and Senator Sharafadeen Alli’s election as governor of Oyo State in 2027. Were you consulted? Yes. We are together. The first time Makinde contested election, we knocked Sanusi’s doors and he supported us without conditions. In 2023, when Makinde sought reelection, though Sanusi was initially reluctant, and he had a good basis to be reluctant because he gave all he had, as he normally does for elections, the only road leading to his resort, which the governor, on his own, promised to fix was left undone. The road is in bad shape as we speak. Though some people will claim that work had started, the pace it is being done is nothing to write home about. And then, Dotun Sanusi, on his own, has put in millions of naira through OYSTROMA to do that road. He partnered with OYSTROMA. item.content:encoded: By Ozioruva Aliu GOVERNOR Monday Okpebholo just celebrated his administration’s second year anniversary in Edo State. So I prefer doing the job than talking so that when you come you see. When they are crying, shouting on social media, it doesn’t bother me because the people that live in those areas know that work is ongoing.
